root_cause.text: The radiotap iterator in `net/wireless/radiotap.c` rejected unknown radiotap bits too early, before the in-namespace lookup, so an undefined radiotap field could leave `iterator->_next_ns_data` uninitialized and later be compared as if it were valid.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `if (iterator->current_namespace == &radiotap_ns) return -ENOENT;` from the branch executed when `current_namespace == &radiotap_ns` and `!align` is detected to after `align` is set, and the CVE description states that “if the undefined field 18 is used, the alignment/size is unknown as well” and “iterator->_next_ns_data isn't initialized ... and we later compare against this uninitialized value.”

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch moves `if (iterator->current_namespace == &radiotap_ns) return -ENOENT;` from the branch executed when `current_namespace == &radiotap_ns` and `!align` is detected to after `align` is set, and the CVE description states that “if the undefined field 18 is used, the alignment/size is unknown as well” and “iterator->_next_ns_data isn't initialized ... and we later compare against this uninitialized value.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Adjust radiotap iterator error handling so out-of-range namespace parsing is only rejected when alignment is actually unavailable, preventing premature `-ENOENT` returns.
intent_record.what: The early `return -ENOENT` check for `iterator->current_namespace == &radiotap_ns` was moved out of the branch that handles an out-of-range or missing namespace entry and into the `if (!align)` block, while `align` is now set to 0 in that branch unconditionally.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the iterator no longer aborts immediately just because the current namespace is the base radiotap namespace and the argument index is out of range; instead, it first treats the entry as having zero alignment and only returns `-ENOENT` when no alignment is available in that path. This changes how the iterator skips or terminates namespace parsing and avoids prematurely rejecting some radiotap arguments.

grouping_result.intent: Adjust radiotap iterator error handling so out-of-range namespace parsing is only rejected when alignment is actually unavailable, preventing premature `-ENOENT` returns.

relevance_review.reason: The change targets radiotap iterator error handling in the same code path as the root cause, specifically when handling out-of-range/unknown radiotap namespace bits. It appears to fix premature rejection before proper namespace lookup, which matches the vulnerability mechanism involving iterator state being left uninitialized.

candidates.rationale: This condition triggers an immediate -ENOENT for unknown radiotap bits in the core namespace before namespace lookup can proceed, which is the premature rejection described in the root cause.
This early return is the direct failure path that aborts parsing too soon, allowing the iterator state such as _next_ns_data to remain uninitialized.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional causes the iterator to reject unknown radiotap bits in the core namespace before the in-namespace lookup can run, which matches the root cause of premature rejection and can leave iterator->_next_ns_data uninitialized.
This is the premature failure path taken by the above condition, aborting parsing too early and preventing initialization of iterator state needed for later comparisons.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this function body. The old parser logic that would reject unknown bits too early has been replaced by namespace-aware handling. In `ieee80211_radiotap_iterator_next()`, unknown bits in the built-in radiotap namespace are explicitly rejected only when `current_namespace == &radiotap_ns` (`if (iterator->current_namespace == &radiotap_ns) return -ENOENT;`), while non-radiotap namespaces are handled by setting `align = 0` and then skipping to `iterator->_arg = iterator->_next_ns_data;` before clearing `current_namespace`. Also, vendor namespace handling initializes `_next_ns_data` (`iterator->_next_ns_data = iterator->_arg + vnslen;`) and selects the namespace via `find_ns()`. This shows the fix is already present and the earlier uninitialized `_next_ns_data` path is not visible here.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this post-commit code. In `ieee80211_radiotap_iterator_next()`, unknown/unsupported fields are no longer rejected prematurely solely by index check; instead the code consults the active namespace first: `if (!iterator->current_namespace || iterator->_arg_index >= iterator->current_namespace->n_bits) { if (iterator->current_namespace == &radiotap_ns) return -ENOENT; align = 0; }`. For non-radiotap namespaces, `align = 0` triggers `iterator->_arg = iterator->_next_ns_data; iterator->current_namespace = NULL; goto next_entry;`, which avoids using an uninitialized `_next_ns_data` as a valid comparator target in the radiotap namespace path. Also, vendor namespace handling explicitly initializes `_next_ns_data` (`iterator->_next_ns_data = iterator->_arg + vnslen;`) before any later use. Since the bug root cause was an early reject before in-namespace lookup leaving `_next_ns_data` uninitialized, and this code now has namespace-aware handling plus initialization, the fix is already present.
